method: Local AD compares point derivative to finite secant; path-average AD asks a separate interval consistency question. Neither agreement alone proves all derivatives correct.
precision_caveat: Float32 native casts/rounding make literal numerical maps discontinuous; quadrature agreement is diagnostic, not a fundamental-theorem proof.

analytic_controls.name: correct_linear
analytic_controls.meaning: correct constant derivative; numerical sanity control

analytic_controls.name: smooth_curvature
analytic_controls.meaning: correct smooth derivative; finite secant differs by epsilon²

analytic_controls.name: continuous_kink_nearby
analytic_controls.meaning: local derivative exists at center; larger intervals cross a continuous kink

analytic_controls.name: continuous_kink_at_center
analytic_controls.meaning: classical derivative undefined at center; agreement cannot validate a unique derivative

analytic_controls.name: localized_wrong_center
analytic_controls.meaning: wrong center derivative can be missed by quadrature nodes

analytic_controls.name: canceling_offcenter_errors
analytic_controls.meaning: center derivative correct; nonzero offcenter errors cancel in symmetric average

analytic_controls.name: discontinuous_forward
analytic_controls.meaning: derivative exists locally but path crossing jump violates continuity assumption
